Product Description:

The Complete Configuration is one of three configurations within PHP’s Modular Peptide System, a modular framework of peptide formulations designed for research evaluation. Configurations represent defined combinations of individual modules (A through E) assembled to provide broader comparative frameworks than standalone module evaluation.

The Complete Configuration combines all five modules within a single integrated framework, representing the full compositional and chemistry-class breadth of the Topical System. By incorporating foundational, targeted, localized, advanced, and composite compositions, the Complete Configuration provides access to every formulation architecture available within the modular platform.

Each included module is independently verified through ISO/IEC 17025-accredited analytical testing using HPLC-UV-MS methodology. Batch-specific Certificates of Analysis are available through the COA-Topicals library.

Research Framework:

  • Complete Topical System architecture
  • All five modules in a single configuration
  • Eight peptides across five structural classes
  • Broadest analytical diversity within the platform
  • Includes every formulation type utilized throughout the system

The Complete Configuration supports multiple evaluation approaches, including individual module evaluation, configuration-based evaluation, and sequential configuration evaluation within a 24-hour cycle. When Phase 1 and Phase 2 are sequenced together, defined separation intervals (typically ~12 hours) between configurations allow the analytical contributions of each to be observed without compositional overlap.

Configuration Characteristics:

  • Combines all foundational, concentrated, precision, advanced, and composite modules
  • Incorporates both free peptides and copper-coordinated peptide complexes
  • Includes serum-emulsion, gel, low-viscosity emulsion, and buffered copper-peptide matrices
  • Represents the broadest concentration range within the platform
  • Includes both single-peptide-dominant and multi-peptide composite formulations
  • Provides access to every major compositional variable engineered into the Modular Peptide System

Position Within The System:

Within the Modular Peptide System framework, the Complete Configuration represents the full modular architecture. It integrates all five modules into a single structured platform and encompasses the entire range of compositional variables the system was designed to evaluate, including peptide structural class, peptide concentration, formulation complexity, chemistry class, and delivery matrix.

Unlike Phase 1 and Phase 2, which isolate specific portions of the modular framework, the Complete Configuration provides access to the full comparative breadth of the system. It represents the highest level of compositional diversity available within the Topical System platform.

System Architecture:

The Complete Configuration spans the principal formulation variables incorporated throughout the Topical System:

  • Peptide Structural Classes: Palmitoylated, Dipeptide, Acetylated Tetrapeptide, Acetylated Octapeptide, Tetrapeptide, Copper-Coordinated Peptide
  • Concentration Range: 0.10% to 0.52% total peptide content
  • Composition Complexity: Single-peptide-dominant through multi-peptide composite architectures
  • Delivery Matrices: Serum-Emulsion, Gel, Controlled-Rheology Emulsion, Buffered Copper-Peptide Serum
  • Supporting Components: Caffeine and Tocopherol

Together, these variables establish the broadest analytical and compositional framework available within the modular system.

Product Name: Modular Peptide System D – Copper-Peptide Complex

Module Classification: Advanced Module

Product Information:

Analytical Composition:

  • AHK-Cu: 0.10%
  • Tocopherol (Vitamin E): 0.20%
  • Total Peptide Content: 0.10%

Product Description:

Module D is one of five products within PHP’s Modular Peptide System, a modular framework of peptide formulations designed for research evaluation. Researchers may evaluate individual modules independently or as part of three structured configurations: Phase 1, Phase 2, or the Complete Configuration.

Module D is a peptide formulation centered on AHK-Cu, a copper-coordinated peptide complex representing a distinct chemistry class within the modular framework. Unlike the free peptides utilized elsewhere in the system, AHK-Cu exists as a coordinated metal complex, introducing analytical variables specific to copper coordination chemistry.

Composition is independently verified through ISO/IEC 17025-accredited analytical testing using HPLC-UV-MS methodology. Batch-specific Certificates of Analysis are available through the COA-Topicals library. Module D is the only product within the framework in which the peptide exists as a coordinated metal complex rather than a free peptide.

Research Framework:

  • Distinct copper-coordinated peptide chemistry class
  • Single-peptide composition with supporting formulation architecture
  • Elevated-concentration advanced module
  • Compatible with Phase 2 and Complete Configuration
  • May be evaluated independently or alongside Module B
  • Includes the system’s only coordinated metal-peptide complex

Formulation Characteristics:

  • AHK-Cu serves as the primary peptide component at 0.10%
  • Tocopherol (Vitamin E) incorporated as part of the formulation’s oxidation-management architecture
  • Buffered serum-emulsion matrix engineered for copper-peptide stability
  • Chelation system incorporated to support coordination-complex integrity
  • Elevated pH range relative to other modules to accommodate copper-complex stability requirements
  • Airless packaging minimizes oxygen exposure and supports compositional integrity
  • UV-protective packaging is particularly important for copper-coordinated peptide systems

Comparative Position Within The System:

Within the modular framework, Module D functions as the advanced composition and represents a distinct chemistry class relative to the other products in the system. It is analytically paired with Module B, as both products utilize elevated-concentration, single-peptide-dominant architectures while representing different formulation and chemistry frameworks. AHK-Cu also appears at a lower concentration (0.02%) within Module E, enabling comparative evaluation of the same compound at different analytical levels across the system.

Copper-Peptide Selection Rationale:

PHP’s formulator selected AHK-Cu as the copper-peptide component of Module D based upon formulation-engineering considerations related to compositional stability. AHK-Cu is the copper coordination complex of N-acetyl-alanyl-histidyl-lysine, an N-terminus-acetylated peptide structure. The acetylation modifies copper coordination behavior, contributing to stable formulation characteristics across the pH ranges typically encountered in aqueous peptide systems and supporting long-term compositional integrity throughout the documented shelf life of the product. This represents a formulation-design decision regarding stability and composition rather than a comparative statement regarding biological or topical activity.

Product Specifications:

  • Primary Peptide: AHK-Cu
  • Total Peptide Content: 0.10%
  • Supporting Component: Tocopherol (Vitamin E) – 0.20%
  • Chemistry Class: Copper-Coordinated Peptide Complex
  • Delivery Matrix: Buffered Serum-Emulsion
  • Packaging: Opaque Airless UV-Protective
  • Batch Verification: ISO/IEC 17025 HPLC-UV-MS

Product Description:

Phase 1 is one of three configurations within PHP’s Modular Peptide System, a modular framework of peptide formulations designed for research evaluation. Configurations represent defined combinations of individual modules (A through E) assembled to provide broader comparative frameworks than standalone module evaluation.

Phase 1 combines three distinct modules within a single configuration: the foundational composition (Module A), the precision composition (Module C), and the composite multi-class composition (Module E). Together, these modules establish a broad-spectrum peptide environment spanning multiple peptide classes, concentration profiles, and formulation architectures.

Each included module is independently verified through ISO/IEC 17025-accredited analytical testing using HPLC-UV-MS methodology. Batch-specific Certificates of Analysis are available through the COA-Topicals library.

  • Foundational entry point into the Topical System
  • Broadest peptide-class diversity among the three configurations

Phase 1 may be evaluated independently as a continuous comparative framework or sequentially alongside Phase 2 within a structured evaluation protocol. When configurations are sequenced within a 24-hour evaluation cycle, defined separation intervals (typically ~12 hours) between configurations allow the analytical contributions of each to be observed without compositional overlap.

Configuration Characteristics:

  • Combines three distinct formulation architectures
  • Includes both single-class and multi-class peptide compositions
  • Incorporates the system’s highest peptide concentration module (Module C)
  • Includes the system’s most analytically complex module (Module E)

  • Provides representation across multiple peptide concentration levels
